text:
maria: Heads up — we saw a sudden p95/p99 jump on hosted text-generation endpoints starting ~02:00 UTC. Small-sequence workloads (seq_len=32, batch≈8) p99 went from ~210ms -> ~650ms. No traffic surge. Rolling window shows throughput down ~20%. cc @ryan @aj
ryan: saw the alert. Any changes deployed around that time? driver/stack updates?
aj: infra rolled CUDA 12.2 patch to a subset of hosts at 01:45 UTC as part of the driver security rollout. I flagged it to infra when we saw other tenants failing matrix kernels earlier.
maria: thanks — I profiled a few slow requests on one host using our profiler (attached below). Stack shows kernel selection falling back to a non-flash kernel path: `triton_matmul_mixed_fp16` and `custom_gemm_v1` instead of `flash_attn_fwd_fp16`. Also see extra kernel invocations around KV management.
li: paste of the profiler snippet: ```
[profile snippet]
kernels:
 - triton_matmul_mixed_fp16 (duration 1.8ms)
 - flash_attn_fwd_fp16 (duration 0.12ms)
 - custom_kv_shrink (duration 0.9ms)
 - triton_matmul_mixed_fp16 (duration 2.0ms)
nvlink: high L2 miss-rate, stall_reason: memory_throttle
```
jess: interesting — the durations you pasted show the triton_matmul kernels dominating time. That suggests the runtime selected an alternate GEMM path for certain micro-shapes. Could be Triton auto-tuner heuristic change with the new driver.
ryan: I ran nsight and saw L2 cache miss spikes (~3x) and DRAM bandwidth saturation on the same host during the spike. There were also other containers doing large-batch dense infer (not our endpoints) around the same time — possible noisy neighbor.
aj: noisy neighbor + driver change could cause kernel autotuner to prefer numerically identical but different kernel variants with worse latency under high mem pressure. I can check container allocation and co-tenancy for the effected hosts.
maria: another data point — KV cache behavior: we saw more frequent `kv_shrink` calls and a higher number of KV merges per request when batching combined slightly different prefix lengths. That increases kernel count per request and amplifies the latency regression on the chosen slow kernel path.
li: so two compounding factors: 1) Heuristic/driver change causing different kernel selection for small seq shapes, 2) Increased KV churn + noisy neighbor memory pressure amplifying the latency.
jess: can we force the selector to prefer flash-attn for these shapes as a mitigation? What config keys do we have?
aj: we have `kernel_selector.overrides` in runtime config. For quick rollback I can push an override: "flash_attn": "force" for affected model shards, and roll back the driver rollout on the most impacted pool.
ryan: tests on a pinned host (manually set override) show p99 back to ~220ms for the same workload. Throughput restored. The override also reduced DRAM bandwidth by ~15% since fewer fallback matmuls ran.
maria: good signal. Can we automate detection? Maybe add a perf-test that runs short-seq microbenchmarks after any driver update and validates kernel selection against expected hot path (flash_attn) for our common shapes.
ops-bot: incident created #INC-2026-412: "p99 spike small-seq kernel-fallback". Pager alert suppressed while mitigation is in progress.
aj: plan: (1) push kernel_selector override to affected hosts (2) roll back driver on 6 hosts in the hosted pool (3) infra to repro noisy neighbor on staging with synthetic dense loads to observe L2 miss interaction (4) add autotest to CI gating driver/kernel selector changes. I'll own 1+2.
li: I'll take 3 and 4 with eng-infra. Also will add a short-running Nsight perf check to our deploy pipeline that validates memory-bandwidth-sensitive kernels.
jess: note: the KV cache merge logic also needs a follow-up — batching heuristics currently create more cross-prefix merges for micro-batches. We should tune the batcher to avoid merging sequences that will trigger extra KV churn for these models. Filing follow-up ticket.
maria: thanks all. For the immediate change I'm rolling the override now to the affected shards; I'll post results in 10m. If p99 drops we can mark incident as mitigated and follow up with infra rollback plan.
infra-bot: override applied to 12 shards in hosted-pool-3. Telemetry: latency delta (pre->post override) p99 650ms -> 230ms, p95 320ms -> 180ms.
maria: confirmed in logs: p99 back to ~230ms, throughput +18%. I'll leave monitoring on for 1 hour before closing.
ryan: nice work. Long-term: we should add a kernel-selection sanity check after any Triton/driver upgrade and consider a more robust selector that factors cache pressure heuristics. Also record per-kernel L2 miss rates in our runtime traces.
maria: agreed. I'll create the follow-ups and link to this thread. Closing for now. :thumbsup:
